blocks.text: The words “when Jesus had finished” mark a transition after a large teaching collection. Matthew uses this kind of ending formula five times to organize major bodies of teaching, though the repetition does not establish one universally accepted symbolic outline for the book.

The divorce exception in verse 9 and the threefold saying about eunuchs in verse 12 remain disputed. They should be read as parts of the chapter’s connected teaching about marriage, children, and discipleship, while preserving the distinctions the passage itself makes rather than forcing them into an uncontested interpretation.
